10.2a — Card Jam Kickoff: Lists & Arrays

Second jam, new data structure: the LIST. Your coins were one number, your inventory was a few bools — a deck of cards is MANY things, in order, changing. The starter ships a card game skeleton (GameManager.cs) with a secret: two of its methods are EMPTY, waiting for you.

Concept Warmup ~15 min

Open the starter's GameManager.cs (find it in the project — the card game scene). Two facts to verify with your own eyes:

  1. It is a singleton — public static GameManager gm; set in Awake — the same pattern your StatManager has used since 2.1. The game manager is THE manager; everything finds it.
  2. It holds about SIX Lists. Count them: the deck, the hand(s), maybe a discard pile, a play field. Every one is a List<Card> or similar. THE WHOLE GAME IS LISTS.

List vocabulary (the exam's, exactly):

Exam pseudocodeC# on a ListWhat it does
aList[i]hand[i]Access the item at index i (starts at 1 in AP, 0 in C#!)
APPEND(aList, item)hand.Add(card)Add at the end
REMOVE(aList, i)hand.RemoveAt(i)Remove item at index i
INSERT(aList, i, item)hand.Insert(i, card)Squeeze into position i
LENGTH(aList)hand.CountHow many items

Socratic

Your deck has 30 cards. You draw the top one: deck[0], REMOVE it, APPEND it to the hand. Why must the removal happen — what breaks at draw #31 if you never remove? (This is also why your coins could never be a List of coin objects — count what you keep, list what you ORDER.)

Pitch ~25 min

The jam task, read carefully: finish the starter's card game as YOUR version — your rules, your theme, your art swap — and ship it in five classes (10.2e build, 10.2f showcase). The skeleton handles setup; the EMPTY methods (Shuffle() and AI_Turn() — verify they are empty in your copy!) are your unit's final boss.

Pitch card (10 min to write, 30s to pitch):

  1. Theme sentence: "a card game about ___" (battles? cooking? dungeon crawling? dueling teachers?)
  2. The core loop: draw → play → resolve → repeat. Which part does the AI oppose?
  3. One twist that makes YOUR game not-just-war: costs? combos? a shared deck? one "cheat" card?

Vote + team (same rules as 10.1a): teams 1–3, everyone writes code, everyone's game has the deck-draw loop playable by 10.2e.

Bug Hunt: List-thinking traps

  1. "My hand shows card 3" — in C#, hand[3] is which visible card from the left? (Count from 0 — the exam counts from 1. Write BOTH answers down; you WILL need both.)
  2. REMOVE while traversing: you remove from a list WHILE looping over it. Why does every item AFTER the removal get visited wrong — and what is the standard fix (loop BACKWARD)?

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Explain the starter's six Lists and what each holds
  • Translate AP pseudocode list ops to C# on sight
  • Explain why draw = REMOVE from deck + APPEND to hand
  • Pitch a card game with a loop, a twist, and an AI
